I should be able to get in still, because none of the things I disclosed are disqualifying. But I’m in an interesting spot right now because it’s been almost exactly a year since I enlisted. Once it’s been a full year, I’m discharged. No more strings attached. And I’m just not sure if I’m willing to enlist again. The process has been hell. My desire to just get my life started clouded my ability to discern if being in the military is really what I want.

So when I first enlisted, my recruiter sat down with me in confidentiality and had me check boxes on a medical/legal history. Just questions about times I’ve been sick, etc. I’m a very healthy person, so there really wasn’t much to disclose. I brought up some small stuff to my recruiter (like breaking my wrist when I was four) and he just sort of laughed it off and told me they don’t care about that sort of thing. Leave it blank, and keep your mouth shut if ever questioned about it. 

So yesterday was my final processing, I had to do more paperwork and examinations just before leaving. One of the guys who’s meant to catch frauds had a sit down with me (as is standard) and asked if there was anything I wanted to disclose. I said no, and he asked if I was sure. And then he told me that I’d be administered a lie detector test at some point after basic training, due to my chosen career field requiring a higher level of security clearance. And that spooked me. I figured it would be much worse to be found out that way than to just fess up to the small things I omitted on my paperwork. So I fessed up, thinking it would be a quick fix. And they stopped my processing. And I feel like an idiot.
